| | |
|---|---|
| **v1 baseline** | `v1.0.0` tagged 2026-07-04 — 187/189 roadmap tasks (~99%); all 8 weekly exit gates met; deployed to Azure Container Apps; retro at [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md); full ledger at [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md) |
| **Current cycle** | **v1.1 — 6 weeks + a stretch week, 2026-07-04 → 2026-08-15 (+ W7 stretch to 2026-08-22)** (planned 2026-07-04 from [context/post-v1-roadmap.md](../context/post-v1-roadmap.md)). Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |
| **Open issues** | **55** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (88 open repo-wide) — `gh issue list --milestone 'v1.1 Backlog' --state open`; the population is stated here because the figure has silently drifted before, so **re-count it, don't decrement it**. (**2026-07-19 — W3 CLOSED: the four build items shipped, wind-down re-homed to W5.** #877 (CI audit gate closed with rationale), #753 → [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927), #910 → [#930](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/930), #904 → [#931](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/931), #591 → [#932](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/932); #588/#590 re-milestoned to W5 (subscription-lapse timeline, not build readiness). **The reviews were worth more than the features this session** — every one of the four found defects the green test suite did not: the #753 409 was leaking grant-scoped suite names AND `pipeline_runs` was still an unhandled-500 path for every polled orchestration connection; #910's `page` mode shipped as **dead code** while client-side throws reported "503 Service unavailable" over a healthy backend; and #904 — a watchdog written to end silent hangs — had an **unbounded Redis read on the watching thread** (#854 verbatim), a guard that **didn't work** (the non-expiring stamp let a *predecessor's* key arm it → permanent crash loop), and an `os._exit` that would abort a live GX run. All 7 fixed. **Lesson recorded: the watchdog's tests were green on all three logic bugs because every loop test ran ONE iteration against a pre-seeded state — the defects lived in state carried ACROSS iterations.** Two process misses, recorded not buried: I pushed #931 with a failing lint gate (ran ruff, saw "1 fixable", pushed anyway), and a branch switch swept #591's files into the #904 branch (caught when its tests failed on the wrong branch; commits split). Filed en route: [#925](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/925) (browse 200-cap), [#928](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/928) (`/pipeline_runs` has no paging — a loop "counted" 20,200 rows against a 211-row table because every page re-read page 1), [#929](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/929) (endemic assert-with-side-effects in wire tests).**) (**2026-07-18 night (latest) — ADR 0037: the asset access model REVERSED, one day after #920 ([#923](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/923) via [#924](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/924), user-directed).** The #920/#845/#901 identity-redaction regime described in the previous entry is **superseded**: asset identity + lineage topology (incl. column pairs) are now visible to EVERY workspace member; the health rollup is **workspace-true** (aggregated over ALL composing suites — one verdict per asset, byte-identical across viewers, pinned by a wire test); the ADR 0027 grants now guard **suite-derived detail only** (composing-suite names/runs/results/samples/incidents — suite-grain 404-no-leak intact; on the asset page hidden suites collapse to a derived restricted count). Asset detail 200s for every existing asset (asset-grain 404-no-leak retired); redacted rows / anonymous nodes / count-only column boxes deleted; lineage-source-health stake gate retired (connections were already workspace-listed). Why: the bootstrap dead-end (a new member saw only 🔒 boxes — discovery-useless) + per-viewer aggregates silently disagreeing between users (the #889 two-verdicts problem). Review batch (4 finder agents): two deploy-skew bugs fixed (old SPA bundle renders every lineage node "🔒 Restricted" without a constant `is_accessible: true` shim on LineageNodeRead — remove after one release; new SPA + old API rendered "Monitored by NaN suites" — total now derives from the workspace-true `suite_count`, one owner, no second wire field read); IncidentsPanel gained the missing "incidents from N suites outside your access are not shown" qualifier (the #828 confident-empty-state class — incidents stay granted while the page opens); one visibility derivation (`effective_permissions` labels AND lists — the second `accessible_suite_ids` round-trip and its read-race removed); single-pass `_latest_outcomes` (rollup and breakdown can't disagree about a run); malformed column-pair ENTRIES now warn (not just whole-value); dead `?? []` fallbacks removed. Deferred, filed: [#925](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/925) (the 200-row browse cap now binds against the widened all-assets population — needs paging + honest tile truncation). #889/#919 updated with the new-model implications. **Deployed + LIVE-VERIFIED same session** (images `b906490c`; migrate Succeeded): browse **byte-identical member vs admin** (22 named rows incl. `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`, yesterday's 🔒 box); member detail 200 with `suites: []` + restricted count 1 while the admin sees the suite named — the suite name provably absent from the member's wire body; UC column pairs (`comment → sentiment`) served to the member; suite-grain `GET /suites/{id}` still 404-no-leak. **The #904 post-roll beat wedge recurred on this deploy** (third occurrence): beat started 05:01:32Z then silence, `last_polled_at` frozen at the pre-roll 04:58 tick — caught by the DB-truth runbook check, cleared by a worker revision restart (ticks 05:19 + 05:29); recurrence + systematic-fix proposal recorded on #904.**) (Previous — 2026-07-18 evening — redacted browse rows shipped + live-verified ([#920](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/920) via [#921](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/921), user-directed) + the harness Snowflake-auth modernization.** Browse now INCLUDES assets monitored solely by suites outside the viewer's grants — as server-redacted rows nested in their real schema group (`DATAQ_DB → ANALYTICS → 🔒 Restricted` where the admin sees `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`): omission asserted "this schema holds nothing else", the #845 falsehood one surface over. One rule, four renderings (full row / redacted row / anonymous graph node / 404), pinned by the UPDATED three-surfaces agreement test + a wire test. The review batch mattered: accessibility now derives from the SAME `_accessible_asset_ids` helper the graph redacts with (a second SQL encoding was the #845/#847 drift class reborn); the disclosed parent path ships **pre-split** (`name_prefix_segments` — a client re-split re-detects the separator on the prefix and files the locked row in a fabricated group); `last_seen` is withheld on redacted rows (watching it tick reveals the hidden pipeline's cadence); one `isRedacted()` discriminator across tree/table/row; the dashboard's Monitored stat no longer counts redacted rows. **Live-verified as Olivia** (interactive Entra re-auth; desktop+mobile): 5 restricted rows correctly nested (ANALYTICS 1, RETAIL 3, ADLS 1 top-level — the no-parent-path shape confirmed intentional), locked rows non-navigating, wire proof `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`/`REFUNDS` appear 0 times in the payload, Monitored still 17, zero console errors. **User Q&A, recorded:** `analytics_probe_analytics_probe` = residue of the 2026-07-12 UC dbt live-verification (dbt's default schema-name concatenation doubling target+custom schema); UC's `reference` schema is absent from assets because NO signal touches it (loaded by pandas writes with no table-grain source, never read by a table-writing query) → the per-connection **inventory/catalog sync** is filed as [#919](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/919). **Harness Snowflake auth modernized (operator + agent):** the user minted a loader PAT (Snowsight; programmatic admin auth is MFA-walled) → KV `snowflake-loader-pat`, validated (`ROYARIJIT04`+`DATAQ_LOADER`), swapped into the dbt job + both Airflow apps; the `--dbt` window then built **17/17 model nodes green** (only the on-run-end GRANT hooks fail — `DATAQ_LOADER` lacks `MANAGE GRANTS`/schema ownership; one-time Snowsight fix in the harness TODO). **Honest SF-pairs status:** real table-write DML now exists (the dynamic tables), but ACCOUNT_USAGE surfaced no `directSources` within a 4h poll — the daily warehouse-lineage beat collects the column pairs automatically whenever Snowflake materializes them; nothing further is wired to wait on it. Harness re-confirmed fully down at the user's ask (5 apps Stopped, 2 ADF triggers Stopped, suspend re-issued on all 7 jobs — the read API doesn't surface suspension, so the idempotent action is the verification).) (**2026-07-18 later — the Enterprise lineage arc: prod 500 + junk-asset fallout fixed (#907/#909, #908/[#911](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/911)), a P1 broken-migration save (#913/[#914](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/914)), and the whole thing live-verified in prod by a two-identity UI pass.** The user upgraded Snowflake to **ENTERPRISE** + granted `DATAQ_READER` the ACCOUNT_USAGE read (Snowsight — programmatic admin auth is now MFA-walled), and `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` went live in prod — whereupon the first real ACCESS_HISTORY pull surfaced two defects: the asset page **500'd** (#907 — the #903 bulk upsert wrote Python `None` as JSON `null`, which passes `IS NOT NULL` and then explodes the reader; fixed in [#909](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/909) as a CLASS: `none_as_null=True` on all six nullable JSONB columns + read guards + a backfill) and the browse **flooded with junk** (#908 — the unscoped account-wide sweep materialized `SNOWPARK_TEMP_*` scratch, the dropped PERF schema, and `adf_stage_import_*` landing tables as assets). **#908's fix ([#911](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/911)) was live-tuned on real captured payloads** (the account's entire history is Stage→Table COPYs — zero table→table DML existed, which itself shaped the design) and the 8-angle agentic review found the deep defect: **the exclusive tier ladder treated two COMPLEMENTARY truths as alternatives** — OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES is the current-state VIEW graph, ACCESS_HISTORY the DML log — so a winning DML tier would have **pruned the entire dbt view chain** on the next snapshot refresh, and an all-filtered-empty pull could wipe the cache. Shipped as a **floor∪DML union** (tier names the richest contributor; empties degrade to the floor, never to a confident prunable empty; the corroboration probe died with the ambiguity it labeled) + 8 more review findings: table-like domain SET not `= 'Table'`, **OR** db-scope (a cross-db edge into scope is real lineage — dropping it is the #845-class omission), quote-aware database fold, snapshot pairs REPLACE / incremental pairs union (stale-mapping + revoked-grant-freeze fixes), the shared `MAX_COLUMN_PAIRS_PER_EDGE` cap, parse-per-distinct-blob, per-query bind assertions, SF column-grain extraction from `objects_modified[].columns[].directSources`; deferred → [#912](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/912) (Snowpark-scratch transitive stitch). **Mid-arc, the #909 deploy silently never landed:** its backfill migration targeted `checks.column_policy` — the column lives on **suites** — so `alembic upgrade head` broke on every FRESH database (caught by the main-branch E2E: the loud failure doing its job) AND the 07:22Z prod migrate execution FAILED, gating the roll (P1 [#913](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/913), fixed [#914](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/914) — safe to edit in place precisely because no environment ever recorded it applied; deliberately no existence guard, a wrong name should keep failing loudly). **Ship + verify:** one deploy carried the whole arc (migrate finally `Succeeded`, beat verified ticking per the #905 protocol); a one-shot scoped refresh pruned prod to **8 clean Snowflake edges** (floor tier, honest degrade note) + UC 6 edges / 4 with column pairs; **634 junk assets** swept via `sweep_orphan_assets` with an injected future `now` (found en route: `retention_days<=0` is the documented OFF-switch, not sweep-all); headless admin-PAT checks green (browse 22 real assets / zero junk, the ex-500 page 200s, `comment → sentiment` live in the API payload). Then a **two-identity live UI pass** (ui-tester + interactive Entra logins as **dataq-admin** and **Olivia**, desktop 1280 + mobile 390): ALL checks pass — junk-free browse (22 admin / 17 member), the ex-500 page renders for both, UC column lineage visible incl. the derived mapping, and the **#845 one-rule proven at the wire as a member**: the out-of-grant neighbour ships as `{namespace:null, name:null, env:null, is_accessible:false}` — an opaque UUID only, with the 🔒 box leaking nothing at either viewport; zero console errors anywhere. UX follow-ups filed, not dropped: [#915](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/915) (the INFO advisory conflates degraded-tier with actually-failed refreshes) + [#916](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/916) (workspace-wide advisory reads asset-scoped — copy tweak). **Honest residual:** SF **column pairs** are code-proven (tests ride the real captured Enterprise payload) but not yet live-visible — the account has never run table→table DML (everything is COPY); a `--dbt` harness window was fired to create real CTAS/dynamic-table DML — and **FAILED: Snowflake's Enterprise MFA enforcement now blocks every password-auth harness leg** (`250001: MFA authentication is required` on the dbt job; `flow_a_snowflake_load` is the same class; DataQ's own PAT-auth connection is unaffected). SF column pairs are therefore blocked on a harness-auth modernization only the operator can do (Snowsight: mint a PAT/key-pair for the loader user; steps recorded in the harness TODO) — after which the daily refresh picks the pairs up automatically (~3h ACCOUNT_USAGE lag). One un-exercisable live case remains: a redacted edge CARRYING column data (no such grant shape exists in the demo data; server+client paths test-pinned). Both prod PATs are live again post-#849 re-mint.) (**2026-07-18 — periodic QA/security sweep → prod deploy `4f8b2ae0` → a 6h silent worker outage (#905) → column-level lineage BUILT + UC live-verified (#901/#902 via [#903](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/903)).** **Sweep:** rule-4a mutation spikes on the newest code, findings filed as [#898](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/898) — `warehouse_refresh.py` **236/239 (98.7%)** once the DB-backed tests were un-skipped (mutmut's copied tree lacks `.env` → every DB-covered module silently reads "no tests"; export `TEST_DATABASE_URL` — the spike's first pass showed exactly that artifact), SF/UC providers ~65% on covered mutants (survivors: static SQL text against stub connections — accepted — plus real gaps in ladder result-shape/edge-filter assertions), frontend Stryker **81.8%** over the four assets modules (`lineageLayout.ts` 66% worst). Security scan clean across Bandit / pip-audit / pnpm-audit / **full-history** betterleaks; the one historical finding (the #849 test's original jwt.io-demo fixture, unpurgeable — force-push blocked) is fingerprint-allowlisted via `.betterleaksignore` ([#899](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/899)) so the periodic full-history scan reads zero and a real leak can't hide behind known noise; targeted #849/#852-class re-verification green (logger-level scrub incl. exported OTel attributes + rendered tracebacks, `azure.core` filter + no-propagate, span URLs path-only, classified-never-raw persistence). **Deploy** (first since 07-13; ships schema_drift #881/#883, monitor registry #880, `monitor_baselines` + warehouse-lineage migrations, warehouse-native lineage #886–#891 dark-by-default, rate-limit prefix buckets #874, 12 dep bumps): pre-checklist green (CI green on the SHA, both migrations up+down tested locally), migrate `Succeeded`, all three apps on the SHA tag, probes correct, one harness `window` (4 min): 5 mockdata jobs green + the `tr_orders_landed` event trigger ran `pl_flow_a_orders` **Succeeded on live Snowflake**, harness auto-stopped. **THEN THE WORKER WEDGED SILENTLY ([#905](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/905), P1):** a transient broker blip 50s after the roll hung the reconnect — beat never ticked ONCE for 6 hours (no retries, no exceptions, replica `Running`, telemetry frozen at 00:13Z) — the third "alive but doing nothing" incident (#852, #854 kin), detected by the telemetry frontier + console cross-check and fixed by a revision restart (beat up 06:17Z, gap recovery swept immediately, backlog dispatched 5/5). The smoke's 00:19Z ADF run was stranded outside both the 15-min poll lookback and the 1-h gap-recovery window — the #828-documented gap, recorded not re-produced. #905 carries the class fix: probeable beat liveness + loud/bounded reconnects + the workspace-wide `last_polled_at`-staleness alert. **Column lineage (#901 + the #902 ladder fix, user-directed, [#903](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/903)):** UC `system.access.column_lineage` pulled on the same watermark/window as table lineage and persisted as a `columns` JSONB **on the edge** (additive migration `a1b2c3d4e5f8`; union-merge across incremental refreshes — never forgets, never regresses to NULL; grain failure degrades with a classified note, never fails table edges), surfaced on AssetDetail with the **#845 one-rule redaction extended to columns** — an edge touching a redacted node collapses to a count-only redacted box server-side (column names are schema disclosure; pinned at the wire). The Snowflake tier ladder now **descends on authorization errors** instead of aborting (#902 — found LIVE: the GET_LINEAGE probe 002003s for a role holding only lower-tier grants like `SNOWFLAKE.GOVERNANCE_VIEWER`; skip reasons + degrade note now carry the real grant-vs-edition cause). **Live evidence:** UC verified end-to-end against the real workspace with prod-parity creds (6 table edges tier `unity_catalog_system_access` + 200 column rows captured → the committed projected fixture the tests ride); Snowflake live-blocked at the grant wall — the PAT authenticates (role-locked `DATAQ_READER`), every ACCOUNT_USAGE tier denied, admin path MFA-walled → the enable steps (Snowsight `GRANT IMPORTED PRIVILEGES` or finer `GOVERNANCE_VIEWER`, + the `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` flip) are the operator's, documented in orchestration.md. Azure note: the subscription is **PayAsYouGo since ~07-13** (no spending limit — awake resources bill real money); runbook probe nit fixed (SPA catch-all serves 200 on `$FE/openapi.json`; the docs gate is `/api/v1/openapi.json → 404`).) (**2026-07-17 — ADR [0036](adr/0036-connection-anchored-check-engines.md) merged ([#894](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/894)):** connection-anchored check engines — every datasource connection offers GX, and a connection additionally unlocks its native engine(s) per its capability set (Snowflake → **DMF**, Unity Catalog → **DQX**, a future BigQuery → **Dataplex**); engine selection is **per check** (`check.engine`, default `gx`, validated against the connection's capabilities; `kind` stays orthogonal to `engine`), superseding the earlier suite-level `engine` toggle. Design-only (index + CLAUDE.md §5 link); DMF is the first native build, DQX/Dataplex trigger-gated. **#858 warehouse-native lineage BUILT end-to-end, all four slices merged; [#858](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/858) auto-closed:** the spike (below) hardened into a shipped feature behind a new **`WarehouseLineageProvider`** seam distinct from the catalog `LineageProvider` — the warehouse returns identifiers in the engine's own case, byte-identical to `asset_identity`, so there is **no fold/enumerate** step and the #823 identity-drift class cannot arise here. **[#886](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/886)** Snowflake provider (`is_incremental=False` → snapshot-diff + **prune**, since `OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` is a current-state view) with the spike's source ladder GET_LINEAGE → ACCESS_HISTORY → OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES: GET_LINEAGE gated by a `0A000` **preflight** (clean-error descent, not catch; per-seed traversal deferred → **[#892](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/892)**), ACCESS_HISTORY **empty-corroborated** against QUERY_HISTORY (silently empty on Standard — a catch would mislabel it), OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES the live-verified floor; review fix — `skipped_tiers` carries the real exception message, not a hardcoded "unsupported on this edition" that was wrong for Enterprise. **[#887](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/887)** Unity Catalog provider (`is_incremental=True` → incremental `event_time` watermark, **never prune**, since `system.access.table_lineage` is an append-only log) with a **6h safety re-scan window** so ingestion-lag rows landing after the watermark aren't lost (idempotent upsert makes the re-read harmless); the watermark never regresses below `since`. **[#890](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/890)** the daily beat task (`refresh_warehouse_lineage`, **dark by default** — `warehouse_lineage_enabled=False`) + a backward-compatible migration (`960d18679639`, 5 nullable additive columns) persisting `lineage_watermark`/`last_refresh_at`/`last_tier`/`degraded_reason`/`last_error` per connection; the recorded reason is **classified, never raw** (same discipline as #828's poll-health). **[#891](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/891)** surfaces tier/degraded/failing on the asset graph — an **INFO**-level advisory (distinct from the failing-source **WARNING**) reading the stored `degraded_reason` / `last_error`, gated behind the same asset-stake rule as `failing_lineage_sources`. Providers are tested against **real captured payloads** (byte-for-byte identity pins per #823, query-column projections committed / full captures gitignored). Two process notes banked to memory: a `mypy (tests)` gate miss (CI runs mypy over `backend/tests` too — #418 — a `str | None` used with `in` without an `is not None` narrow cost one round-trip on #891); and the live-warehouse reads stayed spike-parked (Snowflake trial lapses ~2026-07-25), so **[#893](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/893)** — verify e2e against a deployed warehouse — is filed. **Dependabot batch cleared + the #858 spike ran (user-approved):** all 12 version bumps (#860–#871) merged — the stale branches predated the #878 audit fix, and #861 (mypy 2.1→2.3) needed a manual companion commit aligning the pre-commit hook rev that Dependabot can't touch (the `typecheck-deps-sync` gate would have failed it); mypy 2.3.0 verified clean repo-wide first. CodeQL alert 49 fixed ([#884](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/884) — the deadline-thread helper now records-and-RE-RAISES BaseException, keeping the no-masquerade property compliantly). **#858 spike findings** (issue comments have the full detail): real payloads captured from BOTH warehouses (redacted, parked untracked in `backend/tests/fixtures/lineage_native/` for the build PR) — UC `system.access.table_lineage`/`column_lineage` **work on Free Edition** with `event_time` as the watermark and reads-as-NULL-target rows to filter; Snowflake `OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` captured with UPPER identity byte-identical to `asset_identity`; **`ACCESS_HISTORY` is silently EMPTY on Standard** (45k QUERY_HISTORY rows, 0 ACCESS_HISTORY — the preflight must corroborate, not catch); **`GET_LINEAGE` errors cleanly (0A000) on Standard** → the build's source ladder is GET_LINEAGE → ACCESS_HISTORY → OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES, preferring the clean-error preflight. Snowflake trial lapses ~2026-07-25; captures are banked so the build no longer depends on the window.) (**2026-07-17 — `schema_drift` SHIPPED end-to-end ([#881](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/881) engine + [#883](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/883) UI):** the first stateful monitor kind — one registry entry (#880's seam held: zero chain edits), a session-aware baseline-diff executor (the #794 comparison pattern; runners never see stateful kinds), per-datasource introspection (SQL via one bound-param `information_schema` query, flat-file via Parquet footer / bounded CSV sample, **Iceberg from table metadata — closing #859's drift leg**), `metric_value` = drifted-column count under ADR-0016 bands, dry-run preview that never writes, and the edit-gated re-baseline action (drop-the-row, recapture-next-run — never introspection on the API thread). The review caught two shippers: concurrent first runs both inserting the baseline — the loser's IntegrityError failed the WHOLE run and discarded sibling results (now `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`), and `UPPER()` information_schema matching MERGING two case-variant tables into a union schema no real table has (now exact-spelling-wins + classified 'ambiguous' refusal). Honest-limits documented: CSV dtype-inference noise (ignore_columns/re-baseline is the workaround) and whole-blob Parquet reads (range-read filed as [#882](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/882)). Two CI-only failures taught local-gate lessons now in memory: `pnpm lint` ≠ `tsc`, and version-dependent library inference must never anchor a fixture.) (**2026-07-16 — the W4 schema-drift prep chain shipped in one session:** #427 one-engine-per-runner ([#875](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/875) — review added `LazyEngine`, `pool_pre_ping` for the mixed-suite stale-connection regression, and the `owned_runner` lifecycle) · #592 slice 1, the `monitor_baselines` diff-reference store ([#876](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/876) — migration-safety review caught a missing `gen_random_uuid()` id default that only a real INSERT could surface) · #726+#429 monitor-kind strategy registry + runner-advertised capability gate ([#880](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/880)) · the #859 Iceberg metadata fast-paths ([#879](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/879) — review caught that snapshot `total-records` never nets row-level deletes: a merge-on-read table would have false-PASSED a volume floor; both metadata paths now require PROOF of zero deletes). **CI-wide outage fixed same session (#877/[#878](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/878)):** npm retired the legacy audit endpoints 2026-07-15 (410) and no released pnpm speaks the bulk endpoint (verified vs 11.13.1) — the required audit gate now queries the bulk advisory endpoint directly over the same lockfile graph, proven to FAIL on known-vulnerable versions and fail-closed on parse/endpoint drift; #877 stays open for the revert-to-pnpm-audit condition. The #858 warehouse-native lineage spike is consent-blocked on live prod reads.) (**2026-07-14 — #789 prefix-keyed per-IP buckets shipped ([#874](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/874)):** every per-IP bucket (unauth, per-provider webhook, both `ipall` ceilings) now keys on an address prefix — IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64, configurable — closing the NAT/proxy-pool dilution observed in the #725 post-deploy smoke (200 requests over 11 sibling /32s, none near the cap). ---
name: project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate
description: DataQ's redis:7-alpine pin is a deliberate security gate, not staleness — Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module with an unpatched RCE (#980)
metadata:
  type: project
---

DataQ pins the Redis **server** image to `redis:7-alpine` in both `docker-compose.yml` and `deploy/terraform/azure/redis.tf` **on purpose**. Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module, whose duplicate-HNSW-ID `RESTORE` path is a full RCE (read oracle via `VLINKS ... WITHSCORES` → module-value overwrite → `freeModuleObject()` dispatch) with **no vendor fix** as of 2026-07-24. Redis 7 does not expose the `VSET`/`VLINKS` command surface at all. Tracked at [#980](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/980); found triaging `bikini/exploitarium`.

**Why:** upgrading to 8 would *add* the exposed surface, not remove it — the opposite of the usual "newer is safer" reflex. Nothing automated will raise this: `.github/dependabot.yml` covers pip/npm/github-actions only, **not Docker images**, so a server bump is always a deliberate human edit.

**How to apply:** before bumping the Redis server image to 8.x, verify with `MODULE LIST` on the running container that vector-sets is absent — do not assume the default. Keep `--requirepass` + `external_enabled = false` regardless (the PoC needs an authenticated client, so both layers would have to fail together). Do **not** confuse this with the separate, unrelated `redis` major-version ignore already in `dependabot.yml` — that one is **redis-py** (client), capped by `kombu[redis]`; this is the server image. Related: [[project_postgres_single_role_is_the_mitigation]].

---
name: project_postgres_single_role_is_the_mitigation
description: DataQ's single least-priv dataq_app Postgres role is a security control, not just tidiness — a second untrusted role in the dataq DB enables an unpatched RI cast escalation
metadata:
  type: project
---

DataQ's `dataq` database has exactly **one** app role (`dataq_app`, least-privilege, owns only that DB). That single-role model is **load-bearing security**, not housekeeping. PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check switches to the **referenced table's owner** before invoking an implicit cast on the FK value (`ri_triggers.c`), so a role that can `CREATE TYPE`/`FUNCTION`/`CAST` and holds `REFERENCES` on another owner's table runs its own SQL as that owner — reaching `COPY ... TO PROGRAM` if the owner has `pg_execute_server_program`. Unpatched upstream as of 2026-07-24; found triaging `bikini/exploitarium`. Documented in the `deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf` header and the guardrail table in `docs/progress.md`.

**Why:** adding a second, less-trusted role to the `dataq` database is what would *create* the exposure. There is no patch to wait for and no scanner that flags it — `pip-audit`/Dependabot see nothing, because the risk is a provisioning decision, not a dependency version.

**How to apply:** treat "provision another DB role in the `dataq` database" as a decision that needs revisiting this constraint, especially if multi-tenant or customer-facing DB access is ever considered. Deliberately **no GitHub issue** — it is a standing constraint with no schedulable work, unlike its sibling [[project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate]] which has a concrete trigger (#980).

**Verdict: not impacted.** No code change warranted — this PR is documentation and inline comments only. Recorded because *why* we are safe is not obvious from the code, and two of the reasons are conditions that could quietly stop holding.

## What lands

| Change | Where | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| Redis 7.x pin is a **security gate**, not staleness | `docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/terraform/azure/redis.tf` | The point of use — a future bump is a hand edit to exactly these two lines |
| Single `dataq_app` role is **load-bearing** | `deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf` header | That file already defines the role model |
| Full triage record + 2 guardrail rows | `docs/progress.md` | Matches how #973 recorded the last sweep |
| Upgrade-time checklist | [#980](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/980) | Has a concrete trigger, so it gets a ticket |

## The two constraints

**Redis.** Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module, whose duplicate-HNSW-ID `RESTORE` path is an unpatched RCE. Upgrading would *add* the exposed surface — the inverse of the usual newer-is-safer reflex. `.github/dependabot.yml` covers pip/npm/github-actions only, **not Docker images**, so nothing automated will ever raise this. Distinct from the existing `redis` major ignore in that file, which is **redis-py** (client) capped by `kombu` — the comments say so explicitly, because conflating them is the obvious failure mode.

**Postgres.** PG'"'"'s RI check runs implicit casts as the *referenced table'"'"'s owner*, so a hostile role with `REFERENCES` + `CREATE CAST` escalates to that owner. Our one least-priv role is the entire mitigation. **Deliberately no issue** — a standing constraint with no schedulable work, and a ticket with no action rots.

## Caveats kept, not smoothed over

These are largely **unpatched**, so "not impacted" rests on non-intersection and missing preconditions rather than on being current — no green audit will ever confirm this the way `pip-audit` confirms a CVE. And the repo'"'"'s technical claims were taken at face value; **no PoC was run**. Neither changes the verdict, since non-intersection holds either way.

## Also checked

The one entry that maps onto a *class* in our own code rather than a package: case-sensitive allow/denylists matched against case-insensitive values (the Flowise `node_options` bypass). All three equivalents were verified rather than assumed — webhook SSRF hosts lowercase both the config side and the parsed URL host, and the workspace-admin allowlist matches case-insensitively. All three are allowlists, so they fail closed regardless.

Confirmed absent from the graph rather than eyeballed: Pillow, pycurl, pycares/aiodns, paramiko/ssh2, libarchive, Next.js. `nghttpx` and `docker cp` appear nowhere in the repo.

## Verification

`terraform fmt` + `terraform validate` clean, `docker compose config -q` valid, pre-commit green on all four files. No app code touched, so no test impact.

   e. Agent #5: Read code comments in the modified files, and make sure the changes in the pull request comply with any guidance in the comments.
5. For each issue found in #4, launch a parallel Haiku agent that takes the PR, issue description, and list of CLAUDE.md files (from step 2), and returns a score to indicate the agent's level of confidence for whether the issue is real or false positive. To do that, the agent should score each issue on a scale from 0-100, indicating its level of confidence. For issues that were flagged due to CLAUDE.md instructions, the agent should double check that the CLAUDE.md actually calls out that issue specifically. The scale is (give this rubric to the agent verbatim):
   a. 0: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to light scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.

## Summary of PR #981

**Title:** docs: Redis-8 + Postgres-role guardrails from the exploitarium 0-day triage

**Stated Purpose:**
Triaged the bikini/exploitarium vulnerability repository (~44 PoCs, 12 assigned CVEs, remainder mostly unreported) against DataQ's real dependency graph. Verdict: not impacted. No code change is warranted—this PR is documentation and inline comments only. The PR records why DataQ is safe and documents two security constraints that could quietly stop holding in the future, placing guardrails at the points where they matter.

---

## Files Modified (4 total — comments and docs only)

### 1. **deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf** (+11 lines, no executable change)
- Added a **security constraint comment block** (11 lines) explaining that PostgreSQL's single-role model (`dataq_app`) is load-bearing, not just for tidiness.
- Describes the vulnerability: PG's referential-integrity check runs implicit casts as the *referenced table's owner*, so a role with `CREATE CAST` + `REFERENCES` can escalate to that owner and reach `COPY ... TO PROGRAM`.
- Explains why DataQ is safe: there is exactly ONE app role, not shared with untrusted parties. States the guardrail: **do not add a second role to the database without revisiting this constraint.**
- References the detailed record in `docs/progress.md`.

### 2. **deploy/terraform/azure/redis.tf** (+7 lines, -1 whitespace)
- Added **security pin comment block** (7 lines) explaining why Redis is pinned to 7.x, not upgraded to 8.
- Describes the vulnerability: Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module, whose duplicate-HNSW-ID `RESTORE` path is an unpatched RCE.
- Explains why DataQ is safe: DataQ never issues `VSET` commands; 7.x does not expose them at all. Secondary layers: internal ingress + `--requirepass`.
- Notes that Dependabot does not watch Docker images, so nothing automated will raise this; requires manual review per issue #980.

### 3. **docker-compose.yml** (+3 lines)
- Added **security pin comment block** (3 lines) mirroring the redis.tf rationale for local dev.
- Emphasizes that the Vector Sets RCE is unpatched and that nothing in DataQ uses `VSET`.

### 4. **docs/progress.md** (+22 lines, -1)
- Added a **guardrails table** documenting two standing constraints discovered during the triage.
- **Postgres guardrail:** Single-role model is load-bearing (RI check escalation path). Constraint: don't add a second role without revisiting this.
- **Redis guardrail:** 7.x is a deliberate security pin (Redis 8 RCE). Constraint: don't upgrade without manual review per #980. Notes Dependabot doesn't watch Docker images.

---

## Executable Code / Infrastructure Changes
**None.** All changes are comments and documentation only. No application code, no Terraform resource definitions, no logic, no configuration values changed.

---

## Key Claims to Verify

1. **Redis 8 Vector Sets RCE:** Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module with an unpatched duplicate-HNSW-ID `RESTORE` RCE.
   - Claim: DataQ is safe because it never issues `VSET` commands and 7.x does not expose them.

2. **Postgres RI-check escalation:** PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check runs implicit casts as the referenced table's owner, allowing privilege escalation.
   - Claim: DataQ is safe because there is exactly one app role (`dataq_app`), not shared with untrusted parties.
   - Guardrail claim: Adding a second role to the database without revisiting this constraint would create exposure.

3. **Dependabot gap:** Dependabot's `.github/dependabot.yml` covers pip/npm/github-actions only, not Docker images.
   - Claim: Nothing automated will ever raise the Redis upgrade decision, so manual review (issue #980) is the only guard.

4. **Case-sensitivity in allowlists:** The triage also checked for unpatched case-sensitive-vs-case-insensitive bypass patterns (e.g., Flowise `node_options`).
   - Claim: All three DataQ equivalents (webhook SSRF hosts, workspace-admin allowlist, etc.) already normalize and fail closed.

---

**No test impact** — no app code touched. **Verification status:** `terraform fmt` + `terraform validate` clean, `docker compose config -q` valid, pre-commit passing.
